comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD discuss the integration of AI into computing devices, but they focus on different segments of the market. Qualcomm emphasizes the shift of large generative AI algorithms running on edge devices like mobile handsets and PCs to reduce energy costs, as stated in the target disclosure: 'With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.' In contrast, AMD focuses on how its data center products, including GPU accelerators, are purchased by hyperscale cloud providers to support public cloud AI workloads and generative AI models: 'Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.' While both cite generative AI as a key driver, Qualcomm highlights on-device efficiency and edge processing, whereas AMD highlights cloud-scale infrastructure.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.

comparisons.peer_summary: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs.

While Qualcomm frames local processing as a method for efficiency and contextual use, Broadcom frames private/on-device approaches specifically around mitigating privacy risks associated with generative AI, representing a shared concern for data security in AI deployment.

previous_disclosures.summary: The success of the core licensing business depends on licensees' ability to develop and deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance, over which Qualcomm has no control.

comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue from semi-custom SoC products depends on the success of customers' end products and the company's ability to secure design wins, with no control over customer marketing efforts, meaning actual revenue may not match expectations.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose that their respective revenue streams depend heavily on the market success of products developed and sold by third parties (QCOM's licensees and AMD's semi-custom SoC customers), over which they have no control. QCOM explicitly states it has 'no control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing' of licensee products, mirroring AMD's disclosure that it has 'no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties' and that its revenue is 'directly related to sales of the third-party's products.'

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.
We do not have control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing of products by our licensees, and our licensees might not be successful in these efforts.
Our revenue from our semi-custom SoC products is dependent upon our semi-custom SoC products being incorporated into customers' products and the success of those products.
Moreover, we have no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties, and we cannot make any assurances that sales of their products will be successful in current or future years.
Consequently, the semi-custom SoC product revenue expected by us may not be fully realized and our operating results may be adversely affected.

comparisons.peer_summary: Growth of the software business depends on customer acceptance of newer products and services.

Similarly, Broadcom's software business growth depends on 'customer acceptance of our newer products and services.' While QCOM focuses on the downstream acceptance of licensee products and Broadcom on its own new software offerings, both identify customer acceptance as a critical, external dependency for revenue growth.

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.

comparisons.peer_topic: System-Level Solution Development and Margin Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Development of system-level memory and storage products involves higher per-unit manufacturing costs, longer development cycles, and significant dependence on customer specifications and purchasing volumes, which may result in reduced profits if costs are not offset by higher prices.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Micron disclose dependencies on third parties for product success, though the nature of the relationship differs. QCOM's revenue depends on licensees' ability to deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance, over which QCOM has no control. Micron discloses that its system-level solutions are dependent on 'customers choosing our products over those of our competitors and purchasing our products at sufficient volumes and prices,' noting that even if specifications are met, sales depend on customer selection. Both highlight that their financial outcomes are contingent on third-party decisions and market performance outside their direct control.

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.
We do not have control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing of products by our licensees, and our licensees might not be successful in these efforts.

Even if our products meet customer specifications, our sales of system-level solutions are dependent upon our customers choosing our products over those of our competitors and purchasing our products at sufficient volumes and prices.

peer_results.rationale: NVIDIA's candidates focus on regulatory export control risks and third-party manufacturing supply chain dependencies. These are distinct from QCOM's disclosure regarding commercial dependency on licensee product success and customer acceptance, with no overlap in the specific business driver or risk mechanism described.

comparisons.peer_topic: Materials Supplier Concentration and Geopolitical Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company purchases ~two-thirds of manufacturing materials from five suppliers, some single-source, with no long-term contracts; supply constraints due to extended lead times, limited supplies, or U.S.-China trade tensions could disrupt supply and adversely impact operations.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and AVGO both identify supply constraints as a driver of business risk within the semiconductor industry. QCOM notes that these constraints may incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure supply chain control. AVGO discloses that suppliers may extend lead times, limit supplies, or place products on allocation due to similar constraints, which could disrupt AVGO's operations. Both disclosures recognize the scarcity of supply/capacity as a structural industry risk, with QCOM highlighting the strategic consequence (customer integration) and AVGO highlighting the operational consequence (supply disruption/pricing).

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.
Suppliers may extend lead times, limit supplies, place products on allocation or increase prices, any of which could disrupt supply or increase demand in the industry.
Any such supply constraints could result in loss of revenue opportunities and adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global supply chain complexity and disruption risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's complex global supply chain is susceptible to disruptions from supplier capacity constraints, quality issues, cyberattacks, and natural disasters, which can increase costs, delay shipments, and harm financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and INTC disclose that periodic supply or capacity constraints in the semiconductor industry negatively impact their operations. QCOM highlights that these constraints may incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure control, whereas INTC details that such constraints (including extended lead times and capacity limitations) directly increase costs, disrupt production, and delay shipments for Intel. Both identify supply capacity as a critical vulnerability in the industry.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

▪suppliers extending lead times, experiencing capacity constraints, limiting or canceling supply, allocating supply to other customers including competitors, delaying or canceling deliveries, or increasing prices;

These and other supply chain issues can increase our costs, disrupt or reduce our production, delay our product shipments, prevent us from meeting customer demand, damage our customer relationships, or negatively affect our reputation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Supply chain dependency and material availability
comparisons.peer_summary: The supply chain depends on third-party providers and exacting material standards, with limited sources for certain components. Shortages of raw materials, chemicals, or silicon wafers, along with inflationary pressures and lack of long-term capacity commitments in contracts, may limit bit shipments, increase costs, or disrupt operations. Additionally, reliance on China for rare earth elements poses a risk if exports are restricted.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and MU both address the risk of supply constraints limiting business outputs. QCOM notes that periodic supply/capacity constraints may drive customers to vertically integrate. MU specifies that constraints within its supply chain for materials and components could limit its bit shipments and adversely affect financial condition. Both disclosures link industry-wide supply capacity issues to tangible business risks, though QCOM focuses on the strategic reaction of customers (vertical integration) while MU focuses on the direct impact on its own shipment volumes and costs.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

Constraints within our supply chain for certain materials and integrated circuit components could limit our bit shipments, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial condition.

To the extent we do not have firm commitments from our third-party suppliers over a specific time period or for any specific capacity, quantity, and/or pricing, our suppliers may allocate capacity to their other customers and capacity and/or materials may not be available when needed or at reasonable prices.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company builds finished products and maintains inventory in advance of anticipated demand, entering into long-term supply and capacity commitments which may not be sufficient if revenue declines. Demand for data center products surged in fiscal 2024, and next-generation products are expected to be supply-constrained; the company has increased supply purchases and added vendors, which increases complexity and execution risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA discuss the risks associated with securing supply and capacity in the face of industry constraints. QCOM states that periodic supply/capacity constraints incentivize customers to vertically integrate to secure control. NVDA discloses that it has entered into long-term supply and capacity commitments to address potential insufficiencies, and that during periods of shortage, lead times may be extended. Both companies acknowledge that supply capacity is a finite resource that requires proactive management or strategic shifts (like customer vertical integration at QCOM or long-term commitments/premiums at NVDA) to mitigate risk.

sentences.text: In addition, periodic supply/capacity constraints within the semiconductor industry may further incentivize our customers to vertically integrate in an effort to secure additional control over their supply chains.

While we have in the past entered and may in the future enter into long-term supply and capacity commitments, we may not be able to secure sufficient commitments for capacity to address our business needs, or our long-term demand expectations may change.
In periods of shortages impacting the semiconductor industry and/or limited supply or capacity in our supply chain, the lead times on our orders may be extended.
